historical_timeline.summary: Two operations for benign breast cysts at Mount Sinai Hospital.
Admitted to Doctor's Hospital in New York with psychoneurosis.
Possible first signs of macular degeneration (retrospective suggestion).
Loses central vision; keeps only peripheral sight.
Last unassisted oil painting; letter describing a cloudy left eye.
Died at St. Vincent's Hospital, Santa Fe.

claims.statement: Georgia Totto O'Keeffe was born on November 15, 1887, to Francis Calyxtus O'Keeffe and Ida Totto O'Keeffe at the family dairy farm near Sun Prairie, Wisconsin, the second of seven children.
O'Keeffe died at St. Vincent's Hospital in Santa Fe, New Mexico, on March 6, 1986, at age 98.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Record the death as a fact without graphic detail.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe's mother died in Charlottesville, Virginia, in May 1916, and her father died in Petersburg, Virginia, in November 1918.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The cited chronology does not give causes of death.

claims.statement: In 1927 O'Keeffe was admitted twice to Mount Sinai Hospital in New York for surgery to remove benign breast cysts.
In February 1933 O'Keeffe was admitted to Doctor's Hospital in New York, suffering from psychoneurosis, and recuperated in Bermuda in March and April.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The period term is kept as recorded; no modern psychiatric diagnosis is inferred.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe's eyesight began to fail in 1968.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The documented anchor for the synthetic presentation of macular degeneration.

claims.statement: Early in 1971 O'Keeffe lost her central vision and kept only peripheral sight; the O'Keeffe Museum and the Whitney Museum attribute her vision loss to macular degeneration.
claims.clinical_interpretation: The type of macular degeneration (dry or neovascular) was not recorded in the sources.

claims.statement: O'Keeffe completed her last unassisted oil painting in 1972 and continued in oil with assistance until 1977; she worked unassisted in watercolor and charcoal until 1978 and in graphite until 1984. From 1973 the potter Juan Hamilton was her assistant, and from 1974 he taught her to work in clay.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Shows adaptation to low vision; the modern episode uses it to frame vision rehabilitation.

source_links.locator: Watercolors made with assistants in her early eighties

claims.statement: In a 1972 letter O'Keeffe wrote that her left eye had become much more cloudy and that her right eye seemed to be beginning to cloud.
claims.clinical_interpretation: Quoted in a secondary source from a 1992 biography; the letter itself was not reviewed. Suggests the left eye was affected first.

source_links.locator: Quotes the 1972 letter as cited in Hogrefe's 1992 biography

claims.statement: The first signs of O'Keeffe's macular degeneration may have appeared as early as 1964.

synthetic_episode.teaching_objective: Recognize new distortion in one eye as a possible sign of neovascular age-related macular degeneration that needs ophthalmology evaluation within days; follow intravitreal anti-VEGF treatment with acuity, OCT, and pressure checks under the AAO Preferred Practice Pattern; protect the fellow eye with AREDS2 supplements and home Amsler grid monitoring; and support function, safety, and mood with low-vision rehabilitation, in an artist whose central vision was lost before these treatments existed.

documentation.chief_complaint: Retina evaluation of new distortion and blur in the left eye

hpi.narrative: Ms. O'Keeffe is seen in the retina clinic two days after her primary care visit, where new distortion and a blurred central spot in the left eye were found on the Amsler grid. Over the past few weeks straight lines on her canvases and door frames have looked bent with the left eye, and small print and fine color differences have become hard to judge. The right eye seems unchanged. She has had no eye pain, redness, flashes, or new floaters. She takes no blood thinners and no other medicines. She paints daily and is afraid of losing the central vision she needs for her work.

hpi.narrative: Ms. O'Keeffe returns four weeks after her first aflibercept injection. Lines on her canvases look less bent with the left eye, and the gray spot is smaller. She had a small red patch on the white of the eye after the injection that faded within a week, and no pain, redness, or loss of vision. Her daily Amsler checks show no change in the right eye. She takes the AREDS2 supplement every day and is still painting daily.

hpi.narrative: Ms. O'Keeffe returns four weeks after her second injection, eight weeks after starting treatment. Straight lines look nearly straight again with the left eye, and she can read newspaper headlines and judge color in the studio better than in March. She has had no pain, redness, or loss of vision after either injection. Daily Amsler checks show no change in the right eye. She takes the AREDS2 supplement daily. Her low-vision rehabilitation evaluation took place this month, and the home visit and driving assessment are under way.

hpi.narrative: Ms. O'Keeffe is an 80-year-old painter with neovascular age-related macular degeneration in the left eye, treated with intravitreal aflibercept on a treat-and-extend schedule, and intermediate dry macular degeneration in the right eye. She asked for a same-day visit. Yesterday, on her usual early walk, the sun was low and the ground looked flat and gray, and she did not see the edge of a rock. Her left foot rolled inward and she fell onto her left side on soft sand. She did not hit her head, did not lose consciousness, and had no dizziness, palpitations, or chest pain beforehand. She got up by herself and walked home slowly, about half a mile, with a limp. The outer ankle swelled within an hour. Ice and elevation helped; she has taken nothing for pain. This is her first fall in more than a year. Her daily Amsler grid checks show no new distortion in either eye, and her next retina visit is in about three weeks. She lives alone and was alone on the walk.

hpi.narrative: Ms. O'Keeffe returns for her subsequent annual wellness visit. She completed the health risk assessment before the visit on a large-print form, with the clinic nurse reading the small-print items aloud. Her left ankle sprain from August healed within four weeks with a brace and home exercises, and she no longer uses the cane. That fall is her only fall in the past year; she has had no emergency visits or hospital stays. She continues treat-and-extend aflibercept injections in the left eye with her retina specialist, checks the Amsler grid daily, and reports no new distortion. She takes the AREDS2 supplement daily and no other medicines or over-the-counter products. She paints daily with the task lighting, stand magnifier, and high-contrast labels set up during low-vision rehabilitation. She still drives short local routes by day. Her main concern is staying safe living alone as her vision changes.

documentation.advance_care_planning: Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 20 minutes, with her consent. She had no written directive. Today she completed a health care directive and has named a health care agent; a copy is now in the chart. She values independence and her ability to work above all. She wants full treatment for reversible illness, including hospital care. She would not want resuscitation or prolonged life support if she could no longer recognize people or make her own decisions. She will give copies to her agent and keep one at home.
documentation.follow_up: Physical therapy referral and DXA scan ordered; lipid panel and glucose with the next blood draw. Nurse visit next month for pneumococcal, RSV, and tetanus vaccines. Retina care continues on its own schedule. Next annual wellness visit in one year

referral.question: New distortion and a central blurred spot in the left eye of an 80-year-old painter, suspicious for neovascular age-related macular degeneration. Please evaluate this week and treat as indicated
referral.urgency: Urgent, within the week, because of possible choroidal neovascularization
referral.pertinent_history: A few weeks of straight lines looking bent and a gray central spot in the left eye, with trouble reading small print and judging fine color differences. Amsler grid today shows wavy lines and a small central gray patch in the left eye and a normal grid in the right. Best-corrected acuity 78 ETDRS letters right and 56 left. No eye pain, redness, flashes, or floaters. She takes no medicines, including no blood thinners, and has no known allergies. PHQ-2 1 and Mini-Cog 5 of 5. She paints daily, lives alone, and drives short routes by day

assessment.display: Neovascular age-related macular degeneration, left eye, active
assessment.assessment: Confirmed clinically. A subfoveal gray-green lesion with subretinal fluid on OCT (central subfield thickness 418 µm) and acuity of 55 letters fit active choroidal neovascularization. The picture is typical, so treatment began today on OCT and fundus findings without fluorescein or OCT angiography; angiography is held in reserve if the response to loading is poor or the picture becomes atypical. The first intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg injection was given today without complication

assessment.display: Intermediate dry age-related macular degeneration, right eye
assessment.assessment: Large drusen and pigment changes without fluid or hemorrhage. This eye is at risk of conversion and now carries most of her reading and driving vision, so the AREDS2 supplement is indicated

She has trouble with small print and fine color judgment but remains independent. Right-eye acuity of 78 letters supports short local daytime driving for now, pending a formal driving assessment. Her mood is steady, but vision loss raises the risk of depression

recommendations: Intravitreal aflibercept 2 mg in the left eye every four weeks for three loading doses, then treat-and-extend by two-week steps while the macula stays dry; first dose given today
At each injection visit: best-corrected acuity, OCT, intraocular pressure, and dilated examination of the right eye
Fluorescein or OCT angiography only if the response to loading is poor or the findings become atypical
AREDS2 supplement daily for the right eye (vitamin C, vitamin E, lutein, zeaxanthin, zinc, and copper; no beta-carotene), started today
Daily Amsler grid checks of each eye in turn, with a same-day call for any new distortion or blur in either eye
Call the same day for eye pain, increasing redness, worsening vision, light sensitivity, or a curtain over the vision; large-print instructions given
Low-vision rehabilitation, with a home fall-risk review and a formal driving assessment; referral sent today. Until then, short local daytime routes only
Repeat the PHQ-2 at the next primary care review
consultant_note.communication: Letter to Dr. Ashby today. The diagnosis, the injection schedule, and the warning signs were discussed with the patient, who agreed to treatment
consultant_note.follow_up: Retina clinic in four weeks for acuity, OCT, pressure, and the second injection, and at each injection visit after that. Primary care will repeat the PHQ-2 and review the rehabilitation and driving outcome at the first treat-and-extend visit
